title: web -- Fetch/Search/Open Cheatsheet (URL-as-target banned, grap required for tab-bound verbs)
desc: wkappbot cdp tools (formerly 'web'). Exempt URL-takers: open, fetch, search, tabs, status, close. Tab-bound verbs (navigate, html, url, title, capture, run, file, ocr) REQUIRE grap. OK <grap> on stdout includes cdp:{port} field for port-pinned reconnection.
steps: Exempt (URL/query OK): cdp open <url> launches new tab; fetch <url> raw HTTP GET (no browser); search <query> Google via CDP; tabs, status, close are CDP-port level.
Tab-bound (GRAP REQUIRED): navigate, html, url, title, capture, run, file. First positional MUST be a grap containing cdp:{port}. A bare URL triggers [WEB:<VERB>] grap-required error.
Standard error: 'grap required as first positional. URL-as-target is banned.' Fix: run wkappbot cdp open <url> first, copy the cdp:{port} from OK output, include it in the grap.
Reconnection contract: every tab-bound command emits OK <grap> on STDOUT. Parse stdout for the exact grap to feed the next command.

CDP PORT IN GRAP (mandatory for all tab-bound commands): cdp:{port} pins connection to exact Chrome instance. Example: {proc:'chrome',cdp:9300}. Port is SHA256-derived per project (9300-9995). Only cdp open may omit it.
Title rule: title field emitted only when find match came via title (capped 30 chars, wildcards stripped). Full titles are unstable -- use domain or hwnd for reliable targeting.

Example chain: wkappbot cdp open https://example.com -> OK {proc:'chrome',cdp:9300,...} -> wkappbot cdp html '{proc:"chrome",cdp:9300}' -> wkappbot cdp navigate '{proc:"chrome",cdp:9300}' 'https://...'
web read is REMOVED. Use a11y read with a grap instead.
fetch is for raw HTTP (no JS needed); JS-rendered content needs a11y read on an open tab.
